title: Geometrical Constructions of Purity Testing Protocols and Their Applications to Quantum Communication
abstract: Purity testing protocols (PTPs), also known as Bell state testing protocols, i.e., protocols that decide with high probability whether or not a distributed bipartite quantum state is a tensor product of Bell states, have been proven to be a useful tool in many quantum communication applications. In this paper, we provide geometrical constructions for such protocols that originate directly from classical linear error correcting codes (LECCs), in a way that the properties of the resulting PTP are completely determined from those of the LECC used in the construction. We investigate the implications of our results in various quantum communication tasks, including error detection, entanglement purification for general quantum error models and quantum message authentication.
score_reason: Quantum communication protocol construction from error-correcting codes; unrelated.

title: Binary Reconstruction Codes for Correcting One Deletion and One Substitution
abstract: In this paper, we investigate binary reconstruction codes capable of correcting one deletion and one substitution. We define the <italic>single-deletion single-substitution ball</italic> function <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ \mathcal {B} $ </tex-math></inline-formula> as a mapping from a sequence to the set of sequences that can be derived from it by performing one deletion and one substitution. A binary <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(n,N;\mathcal {B})$ </tex-math></inline-formula><italic>-reconstruction code</italic> is defined as a collection of binary sequences of length <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ n $ </tex-math></inline-formula> such that the intersection size between the single-deletion single-substitution balls of any two distinct codewords is strictly less than <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ N $ </tex-math></inline-formula>. This property ensures that each codeword can be uniquely reconstructed from <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ N $ </tex-math></inline-formula> distinct elements in its single-deletion single-substitution ball. Our main contribution is to demonstrate that when <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ N $ </tex-math></inline-formula> is set to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ 4n - 8 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ 3n - 4 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ 2n + 9 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ n+21 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, 31, and 7, the redundancy of binary <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(n,N;\mathcal {B})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-reconstruction codes can be 0, 1, 2, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ \log \log n + 3 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ \log n + 1 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ 3\log n + 4 $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, respectively, where the logarithm is on base two.
score_reason: Coding theory for deletion/substitution correction; unrelated.

title: A Generic Construction of q -ary Near-MDS Codes Supporting 2-Designs With Lengths Beyond q + 1
abstract: A linear code with parameters <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n, k, n {-} k + 1]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is called maximum distance separable (MDS), and one with parameters <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n, k, n - k]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is called almost MDS (AMDS). A code is near-MDS (NMDS) if both it and its dual are AMDS. NMDS codes supporting combinatorial <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$t$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-designs have attracted growing interest, yet constructing such codes remains highly challenging. In 2020, Ding and Tang initiated the study of NMDS codes supporting 2-designs by constructing the first infinite family, followed by several other constructions for <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$t \gt 2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, all with length at most <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q + 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Although NMDS codes can, in principle, exceed this length, known examples supporting 2-designs and having length greater than <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q + 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> are extremely rare and limited to a few sporadic binary and ternary cases. In this paper, we present the first <italic>generic construction</italic> of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-ary NMDS codes supporting 2-designs with lengths <italic>exceeding</italic> <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q + 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Our method leverages new connections between elliptic curve codes, finite abelian groups, subset sums, and combinatorial designs, resulting in an infinite family of such codes along with their weight distributions.
score_reason: Combinatorial construction of near-MDS codes; unrelated.
key_techniques: subset sums over finite abelian groups

title: Cyclic Scheduler Design for Minimizing Age of Information in Massive Scale Networks Susceptible to Packet Errors
abstract: In multi-source status update systems, sources need to be scheduled appropriately to maintain timely communication between each of the sources and the monitor. A cyclic schedule is an age-agnostic schedule in which the sources are served according to a fixed finite transmission pattern, which upon completion, repeats itself. Such a scheme has a low $O(1)$ runtime complexity, which is desirable in large networks. This paper’s focus is on designing transmission patterns so as to be used in massive scale networking scenarios involving a very large number of sources, e.g., up to thousands of IoT sources, with service time requirements and weights being heterogeneous in nature. The goal is to minimize the weighted sum age of information (AoI), called weighted AoI, when transmitting users’ packets over a channel susceptible to heterogeneous packet errors. The main tool we use is a stochastic modeling framework using either Markov chains (MC) or moment generating functions (MGF), by which we obtain the weighted AoI for a given transmission pattern, which is not straightforward in the presence of packet drops. Using this framework, we provide a lower bound on the weighted AoI for the particular case of two sources, and also an algorithm to attain this lower bound. Then, by using the same framework, we design a cyclic scheduler for general number of sources with reasonable complexity using convex optimization and well-established packet spreading algorithms, and comparatively evaluate the proposed algorithm and existing age-agnostic scheduling schemes for general number of sources (resp. two sources) when the lower bound is not available (resp. when it is available). We present extensive numerical results also involving comparisons with age-aware scheduling to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: New Constructions of Binary Cyclic Codes With Both Relatively Large Minimum Distance and Dual Distance
abstract: Binary cyclic codes are worth studying due to their applications and theoretical importance. It is an important problem to construct an infinite family of cyclic codes with large minimum distance <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and dual distance <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d^{\perp }$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. In recent years, much research has been devoted to improving the lower bound on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, some of which have exceeded the square-root bound. The constructions presented recently seem to indicate that when the minimum distance increases, the minimum distance of its dual code decreases. In this paper, we focus on the new constructions of binary cyclic codes with length <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n=2^{m}-1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, dimension near <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n/2$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and both relatively large minimum distance and dual distance. When <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is even, we construct a family of binary cyclic codes with parameters <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1}\pm 1,d]$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d\ge 2^{m/2}-1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d^{\perp } \ge 2^{m/2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Both the minimum distance and the dual distance are significantly better than the previous results. When <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is the product of two distinct primes, we construct some cyclic codes with dimensions <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k=(n+1)/2$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d\gt \frac {n}{\log _{2}n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where the lower bound on the minimum distance is much larger than the square-root bound. When <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is odd, we present two families of binary <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[2^{m}-1,2^{m-1},d]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cyclic codes with <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d\ge 2^{(m+1)/2}-1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d^{\perp } \ge 2^{(m+1)/2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d\ge 2^{(m+3)/2}-15$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d^{\perp } \ge 2^{(m-1)/2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> respectively, which leads that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d\cdot d^{\perp } $ </tex-math></inline-formula> can reach <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2n$ </tex-math></inline-formula> asymptotically. To the best of our knowledge, for the binary cyclic codes with length <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n=2^{m}-1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and dimension <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k=(n\pm 1)/2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, except for the punctured binary Reed-Muller codes, there is no other construction of binary cyclic codes that reaches this bound.

title: Low-Complexity Algebraic Soft Decoding of Hermitian Codes With Re-Encoding Transform
abstract: Algebraic codes are important in communication and storage systems where soft information is limited and decoding efficiency is critical. Among them, algebraic-geometric (AG) codes are promising candidates to replace the widely used Reed-Solomon (RS) codes. However, their more sophisticated algebraic structure results in high decoding complexity, hindering their practical application. This paper proposes a novel interpolation-based algebraic soft decoding (ASD) for one of the most important AG codes - Hermitian codes. Given a designed maximum decoding output list size (OLS), the interpolation module is constructed, and the decoding is formulated as finding a desired Gröbner basis of this module that contains the interpolation polynomial. The re-encoding transform (ReT) specifically designed for ASD is proposed, enabling the modified basis reduction (BR) interpolation to achieve lower complexity. The ReT is formulated by defining Lagrange interpolation polynomials over the Hermitian function fields and appropriately choosing the re-encoding points. By exploiting the linear code property, the ReT transforms a subset of interpolation points to have zero $z$ -coordinates, which allows a common factor to be extracted from the module basis polynomials, thereby simplifying the interpolation. This paper further proposes an improved ReT employing more re-encoding points. It enables the common factor to have a greater degree, yielding a more significant complexity reduction. This also leads to an early termination for the decoding. Theoretical analysis and numerical results demonstrate that the two proposed ReT schemes efficiently facilitate the ASD for Hermitian codes.

title: New Constructions of Non-GRS MDS Codes, Recovery and Determination Algorithms for GRS Codes
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for constructing a class of non-GRS MDS codes. The lengths of these codes can reach up to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\frac {q+3}{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> (for finite fields of odd characteristic) and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\frac {q+4}{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> (for even characteristic), respectively. Owing to their special structure, we can use the Cauchy matrix method to obtain the necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS codes and non-GRS MDS codes. Additionally, the inequivalence between these codes and twisted GRS codes is analyzed. Furthermore, we analyze the relationships among several existing classes of codes used for constructing non-GRS MDS codes, propose explicit constructions, and discuss the lengths of non-GRS MDS codes based on these constructions. Finally, we design two efficient algorithms to address two main problems in GRS code research, i.e., determining whether an unknown code <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$C$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is a GRS code from its generator matrix <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$G$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, and recovering the key vectors <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {\alpha }$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {v}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> such that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$C = \text {GRS}_{n,k}(\boldsymbol {\alpha }, \boldsymbol {v})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> if <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$C$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is indeed a GRS code. A computational complexity comparison of the proposed algorithms (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(nk+n)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) with that of the Sidelnikov-Shestakov attack (exceeding <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(qk^{2}n+qk^{3})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) shows that our methods offer superior computational efficiency.
score_reason: Non-GRS MDS code constructions are pure coding theory, unrelated.

title: Two Fast Erasure Decoding Algorithms for Reed–Solomon Codes Based on LCH-FFT
abstract: Based on a recently proposed fast Fourier transform by Lin, Chung, and Han, this paper presents two fast erasure decoding algorithms for Reed–Solomon (RS) codes over binary extension fields of length <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$N$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and dimension <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. The first algorithm applies to low-rate RS codes (i.e., <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\frac {K}{N} \leq 0.5$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) and achieves a complexity of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(N \log K)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. The second algorithm applies to high-rate RS codes (i.e., <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\frac {K}{N} \geq 0.5$ </tex-math></inline-formula>) and achieves a complexity of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(N \log (N-K))$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Compared to recent state-of-the-art algorithms, both proposed algorithms achieve the best complexity, resulting in significant throughput improvements in Single Instruction Multiple Data (SIMD) based simulations. Besides yielding new fast algorithms for RS codes, this paper also presents a new interpolation formula, as well as related results, which may be of independent interest.
score_reason: Fast erasure decoding for RS codes is pure coding theory, unrelated.

title: Improved Constructions of Linear Codes for Insertions and Deletions
abstract: In this work, we study linear error-correcting codes against adversarial insertion-deletion (indel) errors. While most constructions for the indel model are nonlinear, linear codes offer compact representations, efficient encoding, and decoding algorithms, making them highly desirable. A key challenge in this area is achieving rates close to the half-Singleton bound for efficient linear codes over finite fields. We improve upon previous results by constructing explicit codes over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q^{2}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, linear over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, with rate <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$1/2 - \delta - \varepsilon $ </tex-math></inline-formula> that can efficiently correct a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\delta $ </tex-math></inline-formula>-fraction of indel errors, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q = O(\varepsilon ^{-4})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Additionally, we construct fully linear codes over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> with rate <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$1/2 - 2\sqrt {\delta } - \varepsilon $ </tex-math></inline-formula> that can also efficiently correct <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\delta $ </tex-math></inline-formula>-fraction of indels. These results significantly advance the study of linear codes for the indel model, bringing them closer to the theoretical half-Singleton bound. We also generalize the half-Singleton bound, for every code <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$C \subseteq \mathbb {F}^{n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> linear over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {E} \subset \mathbb {F}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> a subfield of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, such that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$C$ </tex-math></inline-formula> has the ability to correct <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\delta $ </tex-math></inline-formula>-fraction of indels, the rate is bounded by <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(1-\delta)/2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>.
score_reason: Linear codes for insertions/deletions are pure coding theory, unrelated.

title: An Open Problem on NSC Quasi-Unitary Matrices and Its Application to Quantum Codes
abstract: Matrix-product (MP) codes provide an efficient approach for constructing long classical codes by combining a defining matrix with several shorter constituent codes. Employing non-singular by columns (NSC) quasi-unitary matrices as the defining matrices of MP codes enables the construction of various types of quantum codes. The existence of infinite families of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$N\times N$ </tex-math></inline-formula> NSC quasi-unitary matrices over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q^{2}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> for <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$N=q$ </tex-math></inline-formula> or <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q+2 \leq N \leq q^{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q \neq 2$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is a prime power, was posed as an open problem in the literature and remains largely unresolved. In this paper, we introduce a novel method for constructing NSC quasi-unitary matrices based on a generalized orthogonality relation for cyclic groups. We prove that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(2m+1)\times (2m+1)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> NSC quasi-unitary matrices always exist over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q^{2}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> whenever <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2m\mid (q^{2}-1)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. This result establishes, for the first time, the existence of six new infinite families of NSC quasi-unitary matrices, providing solutions to the aforementioned open problem. The number of such matrices within our framework is also determined. As a key application, we leverage NSC quasi-unitary matrices to construct optimal pure quantum <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-locally repairable codes (LRCs). We propose an effective method for constructing optimal pure quantum <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs from MP codes whose defining matrices are NSC quasi-unitary matrices. Based on this method, we explicitly construct two new infinite families of optimal pure quantum <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs with flexible parameters.
score_reason: Quantum codes and matrix constructions; completely unrelated.
key_techniques: generalized orthogonality relation for cyclic groups

title: Poisson Hail on a Wireless Ground
abstract: This paper defines a new model which incorporates three key ingredients of a large class of wireless communication systems: 1) spatial interactions through interference, (1) dynamics of the queueing type, with users joining and leaving, and 2) carrier sensing and collision avoidance as used in, e.g., WiFi. In systems using (2), rather than directly accessing the shared resources upon arrival, a customer is considerate and waits to access them until nearby users in service have left. This new model can be seen as a missing piece of a larger puzzle that contains such dynamics as spatial birth-and-death processes, the Poisson-Hail model, and wireless dynamics as key other pieces. It is shown that, under natural assumptions, this model can be represented as a Markov process on the space of counting measures. The main results are then two-fold. The first result is on the shape of the stability region and, more precisely, on the characterization of the critical value of the arrival rate that separates stability from instability. The second result is of a more qualitative or perhaps even ethical nature. There is evidence that for natural values of the system parameters, the implementation of sensing and the delayed access for collision avoidance can stabilize a system that would be unstable if immediate access to the shared resources would be granted. In other words, for these parameters, renouncing greedy access makes sharing sustainable, whereas indulging in greedy access kills the system.
score_reason: Wireless communication and queueing theory; unrelated to all interests.

title: Canonical Form and Finite Blocklength Bounds for Stabilizer Codes
abstract: First, a canonical form for stabilizer parity check matrices of arbitrary size and rank is derived. Next, it is shown that the closely related canonical form of the Clifford group can be computed in time <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(n^{3})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> for <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula> qubits, which improves upon the previously known time <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(n^{6})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Finally, the related problem of finite blocklength bounds for stabilizer codes and Pauli noise is studied. A finite blocklength refinement of the hashing bound is derived, and it is shown that no argument that uses guessing the error as a substitute for guessing the coset can lead to a significantly better achievability bound.

title: A New Construction Structure on Coded Caching With Linear Subpacketization: Non-Half-Sum Disjoint Packing
abstract: Coded caching is a promising technique for effectively reducing peak traffic by using local caches and the multicast gains generated by these local caches. Coded caching schemes have been widely investigated, following the seminal work of Maddah-Ali and Niesen. Explicit coding constructions have been proposed for a variety of network topologies with information-theoretically optimal or near-optimal transmission load <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$R$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. An important parameter in these constructions is the subpacketization <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$F$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, i.e., the number of subpackets that each content file needs to be divided into. In particular, the original scheme of Maddah-Ali and Niesen as well as several other variants require <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$F$ </tex-math></inline-formula> to grow exponentially with the number of users <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. In practice, files have finite size and too large <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$F$ </tex-math></inline-formula> yields impractically small subpackets. Therefore, it is important to design coded caching schemes with <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$F$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$R$ </tex-math></inline-formula> as small as possible. At present, the few known schemes with subpacketization linear in <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula> achieve large load. In this paper, we consider the linear scaling regime <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$F = O(K)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and design schemes with a lower transmission load <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$R$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Specifically, we first introduce a new combinatorial structure called non-half-sum disjoint packing (NHSDP) which can be used to generate a coded caching scheme with <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K=O(F)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. A class of new schemes is then obtained by constructing NHSDP. Theoretical analysis and numerical results demonstrate that 1) in comparison to existing schemes with linear subpacketization, the proposed scheme achieves a lower load; 2) proposed scheme also attains a lower load than some existing schemes with polynomial subpacketization in some cases; and 3) proposed scheme achieves load values comparable to those of existing schemes with exponential subpacketization in some cases. Furthermore, the newly introduced concept of NHSDP is closely related to classical combinatorial structures, including cyclic difference packings (CDP), non-three-term arithmetic progressions (NTAP), and perfect hash families (PHF). These relationships underscore the significance of NHSDP as a combinatorial structure of independent interest in the field of combinatorial design, even beyond its application to coded caching.

title: Universal Framework for Parametric Constrained Coding
abstract: Constrained coding is a subfield of coding theory that tackles efficient communication under constraints. While fixed constraints (e.g., a fixed set of substrings may not appear in transmitted messages) have a general optimal solution, there is increasing demand for supporting parametric constraints that are dependent on the message length and portray some property (e.g., no $\log (n)$ consecutive zeros). Several works have tackled such parametric constraints through iterative algorithms, yet they require complex constructions specific to each constraint to guarantee convergence through monotonic progression. In this paper, we propose a universal framework for tackling any parametric constraint problem through a new simple iterative algorithm. By reducing an execution of this iterative algorithm to an acyclic graph traversal, we prove a surprising result that guarantees convergence with low average time complexity even without requiring any monotonic progression. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this universal framework, with much of our focus on the special case of single-symbol redundancy, while also considering a variety of both local and global constraints. We begin by exploring the local constraints involving illegal substrings of variable length, where the construction essentially iteratively replaces forbidden windows. This local algorithm is applied to various fundamental constraints, achieving state-of-the-art results through simple adaptations of the universal algorithm. We then continue by exploring global constraints, and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed construction on repeat-free encoding, reverse-complement encoding and DNA data storage. Overall, the proposed framework generates state-of-the-art constructions with significant ease while also enabling the simultaneous integration of multiple constraints for the first time.

title: Byzantine-Eavesdropper Alliance: How to Achieve Symmetric Privacy in Quantum X -Secure B -Byzantine E -Eavesdropped U -Unresponsive T -Colluding PIR?
abstract: We consider the quantum <italic>symmetric</italic> private information retrieval (QSPIR) problem in a system with <italic>N</italic> databases and <italic>K</italic> messages, with <italic>U</italic> unresponsive servers, <italic>T</italic>-colluding servers, and <italic>X</italic>-security parameter, under several fundamental threat models. In the first model, there are <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {E}_{1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> eavesdropped links in the uplink direction (the direction from the user to the <italic>N</italic> servers), <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {E}_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> eavesdropped links in the downlink direction (the direction from the servers to the user), where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|\mathcal {E}_{1}|, |\mathcal {E}_{2}| \leq E$ </tex-math></inline-formula>; we coin this eavesdropper setting as <italic>dynamic</italic> eavesdroppers. We show that super-dense coding gain can be achieved for some regimes. In the second model, we consider the case with Byzantine servers, i.e., servers that can coordinate to devise a plan to harm the privacy and security of the system together with static eavesdroppers, by listening to the same links in both uplink and downlink directions. It is important to note the considerable difference between the two threat models, since the eavesdroppers can take huge advantage of the presence of the Byzantine servers. Unlike the previous works in SPIR with Byzantine servers, that assume that the Byzantine servers can send only random symbols independent of the stored messages, we follow the original definition of Byzantine servers inPIR proposed by Banawan-Ulukus, where the Byzantine servers can send symbols that can be functions of the storage, queries, as well as the random symbols in a way that can produce worse harm to the system. In the third and the most novel threat model, we consider the presence of Byzantine servers and dynamic eavesdroppers together. We show that having dynamic eavesdroppers along with Byzantine servers in the same system model creates more threats to the system than having static eavesdroppers with Byzantine servers. This is the first work that considers the quantum version of unresponsive and eavesdropped threat model. In addition, this is the first work, classical or quantum, that considers the presence of Byzantine servers together with eavesdroppers in the same system model (static or dynamic eavesdroppers). Another layer of difficulty that we handle in this work stems from the <italic>symmetric</italic> privacy requirement in the presence of Byzantine servers, which by itself has never been studied before in classical or quantum variations; here the Byzantine servers may attempt to leak information about undesired messages to the user, which is not allowed in SPIR.

title: Locally Repairable Convertible Codes: Improved Lower Bound and General Construction
abstract: In this paper, we consider convertible codes with the locally repairable property. We present an improved lower bound on access cost associated with <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta \geqslant 2)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-locality, which extends the known lower bound only related to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$r$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. We then provide a general construction of convertible codes with optimal access cost which shows that these codes can have super-linear length or maximally recoverable property. Furthermore, we propose explicit constructions of convertible codes with the final code achieving super-linear length or maximally recoverable property when the initial codes have super-linear length or maximally recoverable property respectively. Specifically, compared with known constructions, our construction is applicable to the case <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\delta \gt 2$ </tex-math></inline-formula> for the first time.

title: On Many-to-One Mappings Over Finite Fields
abstract: We introduce the definition of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings between two finite sets, which unifies and generalizes the definitions of 2-to-1 and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings in recent literature. We also characterize these <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings in terms of the generalized local criterion and thus provide three generic constructions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings, which unify and generalize the previous known constructions. Using these constructions, the problem whether <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$x^{r} h(x^{s})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 on the multiplicative group <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}^{*}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is converted into that whether an associated polynomial <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$x^{r_{1}} h(x)^{s_{1}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 on the order <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\ell $ </tex-math></inline-formula> subgroup <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$U_{\ell }$ </tex-math></inline-formula> of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}^{*}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m_{2} = m / (r, s)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\ell = (q-1) / s$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Furthermore, the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 property of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$x^{r_{1}} h(x)^{s_{1}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$U_{\ell }$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is studied in detail in four different cases. In addition, a recursive construction of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings from <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-to-1 mappings is proposed.

title: Some Classes of Punctured Codes
abstract: For <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$i\in \{1,2\}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, let <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}_{i}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> be an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n,k_{i},d_{i}]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cyclic code over the finite field <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. The <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(\mathcal {C}_{1},\mathcal {C}_{1}+\mathcal {C}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-construction produces <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[2n,k_{1}+k_{2}]_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> quasi-cyclic (QC) codes with index 2, which have three types of codewords, i.e., <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(c_{1},c_{1})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(0,c_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(c_{1},c_{1}+c_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. In this paper, we firstly investigate the weight distributions of the QC codes <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(\mathcal {C}_{1},\mathcal {C}_{1}+\mathcal {C}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. By deleting coordinates on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}_{1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}_{1}+\mathcal {C}_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we obtain several classes of linear codes with the forms <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(\mathcal {C}^{T_{p}},\mathcal {C}_{1}+\mathcal {C}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(\mathcal {C}^{T_{p}},(\mathcal {C}_{1}+\mathcal {C}_{2})^{T_{s}})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$T_{p}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$T_{s}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> are sets of coordinates, and determine their weight enumerators in some cases. All these codes are optimal with respect to the Griesmer bound, and can produce new few-weight linear codes after comparing with some recent works. Finally, we analyze the minimum locality of the duals of some punctured codes. Two classes of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-optimal and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-optimal locally recoverable codes are constructed.

title: Pretty Good Simulation of All Quantum Measurements by Projective Measurements
abstract: In quantum theory, general measurements are described by Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs). We show that for any <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$d$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-dimensional system, applying depolarizing noise with constant visibility renders <italic>any</italic> POVM simulable by a randomized implementation of projective measurements—without auxiliary systems. This constrains the asymptotic advantage of POVMs over projective measurements in tasks such as state discrimination, shadow tomography, and quantum metrology. We further improve known bounds on the visibility range for which noisy pure two-qudit states admit local hidden-variable models under general measurements. As a byproduct, we obtain asymptotically tight bounds on the critical visibility for joint measurability of all POVMs. Technically, we leverage recent results in POVM simulation, the Kadison–Singer problem, and introduce a “dimension-deficient” Naimark theorem. Additionally, we demonstrate that general <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2N$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-qubit circuits can be simulated via randomization over circuits on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$N+1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> qubits, with constant overhead, suggesting new avenues for circuit knitting in near-term quantum architectures.

title: Infinite Families of Optimal Codes Over Non-Unital Non-Commutative Rings From Simplicial Complexes
abstract: In this paper, several infinite families of codes over the extension of non-unital non-commutative rings are constructed utilizing general simplicial complexes. Thanks to the special structure of the defining sets, the principal parameters of these codes are characterized. Specially, when the employed simplicial complexes are generated by a single maximal element, we determine their Lee weight distributions completely. Furthermore, by considering the Gray image codes and the corresponding subfield-like codes, numerous of linear codes over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> are also obtained, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is a prime power. Certain conditions are given to ensure the above linear codes are (Hermitian) self-orthogonal in the case of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q=2,3,4$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. It is noteworthy that most of the derived codes over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> satisfy the Ashikhmin-Barg’s condition for minimality. Besides, we obtain two infinite families of distance-optimal codes over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> with respect to the Griesmer bound. By puncturing the Gray image codes and subfield-like codes, several classes of projective codes are presented.
score_reason: Coding theory over non-unital non-commutative rings is unrelated to the researcher's interests.

title: The Generalized Trifference Problem
abstract: We study the problem of finding the largest number <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$T(n, m)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> of ternary vectors of length <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula> such that for any three distinct vectors there are at least <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> coordinates where they pairwise differ. This problem is a special case of the perfect <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-hashing problem in theoretical computer science, corresponding to the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k=3$ </tex-math></inline-formula> case. For <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m = 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we get the classical trifference problem which is wide open. We prove upper and lower bounds on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$T(n, m)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> for various ranges of the parameter <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and determine the phase transition threshold on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m=m(n)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$T(n, m)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> jumps from constant to exponential in <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. By relating the linear version of this problem to a problem on blocking sets in finite geometry, we give explicit constructions and probabilistic lower bounds. We also compute the exact values of this function and its linear variation for small parameters. Moreover, we relate the trifference problem to the sunflower conjecture.

title: Cyclic Codes With Even Length From the (C <sub>1</sub> + C <sub>2</sub> ,C <sub>1</sub> – C <sub>2</sub> ) Construction
abstract: Few-weight cyclic codes are widely used in the area of communication and cryptography due to their good algebraic structure. Let <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathcal {C}}_{1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> be an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n,s_{1},d_{1}]_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cyclic code and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathcal {C}}_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> be an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n,s_{2},d_{2}]_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> negacyclic code. Define <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$({\mathcal {C}}_{1}+{\mathcal {C}}_{2},{\mathcal {C}}_{1}-{\mathcal {C}}_{2})=\{(c_{1}+c_{2},c_{1}-c_{2})|c_{1}\in {\mathcal {C}}_{1},c_{2}\in {\mathcal {C}}_{2}\}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Notice that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$({\mathcal {C}}_{1}+{\mathcal {C}}_{2},{\mathcal {C}}_{1}-{\mathcal {C}}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[2n,k\leq s_{1}+s_{2}]_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> cyclic code. In this paper, based on some structural properties of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$({\mathcal {C}}_{1}+{\mathcal {C}}_{2},{\mathcal {C}}_{1}-{\mathcal {C}}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we determine the weight distributions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$({\mathcal {C}}_{1}+{\mathcal {C}}_{2},{\mathcal {C}}_{1}-{\mathcal {C}}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> in some special cases by Gauss sums. Several classes of distance-optimal or almost distance-optimal few-weight cyclic codes with respect to the Griesmer bound are derived. Furthermore, by some puncturing and shortening techniques on the cyclic code <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$({\mathcal {C}}_{1}+{\mathcal {C}}_{2},{\mathcal {C}}_{1}-{\mathcal {C}}_{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we derive six classes of distance-optimal or almost distance-optimal linear codes. At the end, we construct some explicit distance-optimal or best known few-weight cyclic codes with even length. As an application, we determine the locality of punctured and shortened codes, and obtained several families of distance-optimal or dimension-optimal locally recoverable codes.

title: On MDS Convertible Codes in the Merge Regime
abstract: In large-scale distributed storage systems, erasure coding is employed to ensure reliability against disk failures. Recent work by Kadekodi et al. demonstrates that adapting code parameters to varying disk failure rates can lead to significant storage savings without compromising reliability. Such adaptations, known as <italic>code conversions</italic>, motivate the design of <italic>convertible codes</italic>, which enable efficient transformations between codes of different parameters. In this work, we study the setting in which <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda $ </tex-math></inline-formula> codewords of an initial <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n^{I} = k^{I} + r^{I},{\,}k^{I}]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> MDS code are merged into a single codeword of a final <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$[n^{F} = \lambda k^{I} + r^{F},{\,}k^{F} = \lambda k^{I}]$ </tex-math></inline-formula> MDS code. We begin by presenting three constructions that achieve optimal <italic>access cost</italic>, defined as the total number of disks accessed during the conversion process. The first two constructions apply when <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda \leq r^{I}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and impose specific divisibility conditions on <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$r^{I}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and the field size <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. These schemes minimize both the per-symbol and the overall access cost. The third construction, which builds on a prior scheme by Kong, achieves minimal access cost while supporting arbitrary parameter regimes. All three constructions require field sizes that are linear in the final code length, and notably, the third construction achieves a field size that matches the lower bound implied by the MDS conjecture in almost all cases. In addition, we propose a construction that optimizes the <italic>bandwidth cost</italic>, defined as the total number of symbols transmitted during conversion. This scheme is a refinement of Maturana and Rashmi’s bandwidth-optimal construction based on the piggybacking framework, and achieves reduced sub-packetization.

title: Polyphase Sequences With Flexible Zero-Ambiguity-Zone Configurations for Integrated Sensing and Communications
abstract: This paper develops the theory and constructions of polyphase zero-ambiguity-zone (ZAZ) sequences for ISAC waveforms, enabling the ZAZ shape to be designed over delay–Doppler regions of interest and supporting flexible (including multi-mode) sensing–communication operation. We first prove that a polyphase sequence with an optimal rectangular auto-ZAZ must be a member of some uncorrelated optimal ZCZ sequence family, and conversely, any member of an uncorrelated optimal ZCZ sequence family has an optimal rectangular auto-ZAZ. We generalize the optimality condition on the rectangular ZAZ to that on centrally symmetric convex ZAZs in general. We propose some constructions of families of polyphase sequences with a strictly or asymptotically optimal rectangular ZAZ, and asymptotically optimal rhombic or hexagonal ZAZ from the flexible ZAZ configuration.

title: Constructions of Combinatorial Neural Codes With Asymmetric Discrepancy
abstract: The recent work by Cotardo and Ravagnani (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, vol. 68, no. 5, pp. 2941-2950, May 2022) introduced a class of binary codes endowed with asymmetric discrepancy, which are referred to as Combinatorial Neural codes (CN codes), and are motivated by theoretical neuroscience. The applications in binary asymmetric memoryless channel and neuroscience have spurred interest in constructing binary codes and analyzing the error-correction capabilities under asymmetric discrepancy. In this paper, we first characterize equidistant CN codes and propose several constructions of (equidistant) CN codes based on the Hadamard codes and punctured Hadamard codes. For a binary linear code <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathcal {C}}\subseteq {\mathrm {GF}}(2)^{n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we then analyze the minimum asymmetric discrepancy of the nonzero subset <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathcal {C}}\backslash \left \{\mathbf {0}\right \}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, the coset <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathbf {u}}+{\mathcal {C}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>(<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathbf {u}}\in {\mathrm {GF}}(2)^{n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>), and the union <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\mathcal {C}}\cup \left ({{\mathbf{1}+{\mathcal {C}}}}\right)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbf{0}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>denotes the all-zero vector and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbf{1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>the all-one vector. Based on these results, we completely determine the exact parameters for several classes of CN codes by combining simplex codes or projective 2-weight codes.

title: The Covering Radius of Group Codes
abstract: Group codes form an important class of spherical codes, consisting of a single orbit under a subgroup of the orthogonal group. They have been studied by (Mittelholzer-Lahtonen, 1996) in the case of Coxeter groups for their packing radius. We study them here for the same groups, with respect to their covering radius. An exact algorithm to determine their covering radii is derived, based on geometric ideas, and applied to tabulate their values in dimensions up to 8. The values of the covering radii are compared to the sphere covering bound, and to the bounds in (Fazekas-Levenshtein, 1995) and (Boyvalenkov-Stoyanova, 2021) on the covering radius of spherical designs with given strength. For many sizes of codes, our codes are reasonably sparse sphere coverings, and the only known in these dimensions.

title: The Voronoi Spherical CDF for Lattices and Linear Codes: New Bounds for Quantization and Coding
abstract: For a lattice/linear code, we define the Voronoi spherical cumulative density function (CDF) as the CDF of the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\ell _{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-norm/Hamming weight of a random vector uniformly distributed over the Voronoi cell. Using the first moment method together with a simple application of Jensen’s inequality, we develop lower bounds on the expected Voronoi spherical CDF of a random lattice/linear code. Our bounds are valid for any finite dimension and are quite close to a ball-based lower bound. They immediately translate to new non-asymptotic upper bounds on the normalized second moment and the error probability of a random lattice over the additive white Gaussian noise channel, as well as new non-asymptotic upper bounds on the Hamming distortion and the error probability of a random linear code over the binary symmetric channel. In particular, we show that for most lattices in <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {R}^{n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> the second moment is greater than that of a Euclidean ball with the same covolume only by a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\left ({{1+O\left ({{\frac {1}{n}}}\right)}}\right)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> multiplicative factor. Similarly, for most linear codes in <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{2}^{n}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> the expected Hamming distortion is greater than that of a corresponding Hamming ball only by an additive universal constant.

title: Recursive Decoding of Projective Reed–Muller Codes
abstract: We give a recursive decoding algorithm for projective Reed-Muller codes making use of a decoder for affine Reed-Muller codes. We determine the number of errors that can be corrected in this way, which is the current highest for decoders of projective Reed-Muller codes. We determine the degrees for which we can decode up to the error correction capability of these codes, and we compute the order of complexity of the algorithm, given by that of the chosen decoder for affine Reed-Muller codes. We also show how the decoder behaves when increasing the number of variables and the size of the field.

title: The Minimum Distance of Three Classes of Primitive BCH Codes and Certain Classes of Cyclic Codes
abstract: In this article, we determine the exact minimum distance of three distinct classes of primitive BCH codes. We also compute the minimum distance of certain classes of cyclic codes whose defining sets are unions of non-consecutive cyclotomic cosets. Furthermore, we address open problems proposed by Ding regarding the minimum distance of cyclic codes obtained from Dickson polynomials.

title: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Input/Output
abstract: Usual scenarios of fault-tolerant computation are concerned with the fault-tolerant realization of quantum algorithms that compute classical functions, such as Shor’s algorithm for factoring. In particular, this means that input and output to the quantum algorithm are classical. In contrast to stand-alone single-core quantum computers, in many distributed scenarios, quantum information might have to be passed on from one quantum information processing system to another one, possibly via noisy quantum communication channels with noise levels above fault-tolerant thresholds. In such situations, quantum information processing devices will have quantum inputs, quantum outputs or even both, which pass qubits among each other. Working in the fault-tolerant framework of [Kitaev, 1997], we show that any quantum circuit with quantum input and output can be transformed into a fault-tolerant circuit that produces the ideal circuit with some controlled noise applied at the input and output. The framework allows the direct composition of the statements, enabling versatile future applications. We illustrate this with a concrete application, namely, communication over a noisy channel with faulty encoding and decoding operations [Christandl and Müller-Hermes, 2024]. For communication codes with linear minimum distance, we construct fault-tolerant encoders and decoders for general noise (including coherent errors). For the weaker, but standard model of local stochastic noise, we obtain fault-tolerant encoders and decoders for any communication code that can correct a constant fraction of random errors.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Aperiodic and Periodic Sequence Sets With Low Ambiguity Zone Through Locally Perfect Nonlinear Functions
abstract: Low ambiguity zone (LAZ) sequences play a crucial role in modern integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In this paper, we introduce a novel class of functions known as locally perfect nonlinear functions (LPNFs). By utilizing LPNFs and interleaving techniques, we propose three new classes of both periodic and aperiodic LAZ sequence sets with flexible parameters. The proposed periodic and aperiodic LAZ sequence sets are asymptotically optimal with respect to the periodic and aperiodic lower AF bounds, respectively, which were proposed recently in [IEEE J. Sel. Areas Commun. 40 (6): 1809-1822]. Notably, the aperiodic LAZ sequence sets are the first such sequence sets in the literature that satisfy the bound. Finally, we demonstrate that the proposed sequence sets are cyclically distinct.
score_reason: Sequence design for ISAC via nonlinear functions; purely coding/information theory.

title: New Constructions of Locally Perfect Nonlinear Functions and Their Application to Sequence Sets With Low Ambiguity Zone
abstract: Low Ambiguity Zone (LAZ) sequences are essential in modern integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Recently, locally perfect nonlinear functions (LPNFs) have been employed to design LAZ sequences with flexible parameters. In this work, we propose three new classes of LPNFs and use them to construct LAZ sequences that offer additional flexible parameters. Notably, all the proposed LAZ sequences are asymptotically optimal with respect to the Ye-Zhou-Fan-Liu-Lei-Tang bounds derived in [IEEE J. Sel. Areas Commun. 40(6), pp. 1809-1822, 2022].

title: Construction of MRD Codes Based on Circular-Shift Operations
abstract: Most well-known constructions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(N \times n, q^{Nk}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> maximum rank distance (MRD) codes rely on the arithmetic of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q^{N}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, whose increasing complexity with larger <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$N$ </tex-math></inline-formula> hinders parameter selection and practical implementation. In this work, based on circular-shift operations, we present a construction of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(J \times n, q^{Jk}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> MRD codes with efficient encoding, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$J$ </tex-math></inline-formula> equals to the Euler’s totient function of a defined <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$L$ </tex-math></inline-formula> subject to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\gcd (q, L) = 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. The proposed construction is performed entirely over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbf {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and avoids the arithmetic of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbf {F}_{q^{J}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Furthermore, we characterize the constructed MRD codes, Gabidulin codes and twisted Gabidulin codes using a set of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-linearized polynomials over the row vector space <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}^{N}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, and clarify the inherent difference and connection among these code families. Specifically, for the case <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$J \neq m_{L}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m_{L}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> denotes the multiplicative order of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula> modulo <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$L$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we show that the proposed MRD codes, in a family of settings, are different from any Gabidulin code and any twisted Gabidulin code. For the case <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$J = m_{L}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we prove that every constructed <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(J \times n, q^{Jk}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> MRD code coincides with a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(J \times n, q^{Jk}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> Gabidulin code, so that an equivalent circular-shift-based construction of Gabidulin codes is obtained which operates directly over <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and avoids the arithmetic of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{q^{J}}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. In addition, we prove that under some parameter settings, the constructed MRD codes are equivalent to a generalization of Gabidulin codes obtained by summing and concatenating several <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(m_{L} \times n, q^{m_{L}k}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> Gabidulin codes. When <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q=2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$L$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is prime and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n\leq m_{L}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, it is analyzed that generating a codeword of the proposed <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$((L-1) \times n, 2^{(L-1)k}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> MRD codes requires <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(nkL)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> exclusive OR (XOR) operations, while generating a codeword of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$((L-1) \times n, 2^{(L-1)k}, d)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> Gabidulin codes, based on customary construction, requires <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(nkL^{2})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> XOR operations.
score_reason: MRD code construction; pure algebraic coding theory, unrelated.

title: Further Results on Bent Partitions
abstract: Bent partitions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(p)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> play an important role in constructing (vectorial) bent functions, partial difference sets, and association schemes, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(p)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> denotes an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-dimensional vector space over the finite field <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {F}_{p}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is an even positive integer, and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is a prime. It is a challenging open problem whether the depth of any bent partition of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(p)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is always a power of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Notably, the depths of all currently known bent partitions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(p)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> are powers of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. In this paper, we prove that for a bent partition <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\Gamma $ </tex-math></inline-formula> of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(p)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> for which all the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-ary bent functions generated by <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\Gamma $ </tex-math></inline-formula> are regular or all are weakly regular but not regular, the depth of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\Gamma $ </tex-math></inline-formula> must be a power of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$p$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. We present new constructions of bent partitions that (do not) correspond to vectorial dual-bent functions. In particular, a new construction of vectorial dual-bent functions is provided. Additionally, for general bent partitions of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$V_{n}^{(2)}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we establish a characterization in terms of Hadamard matrices.

title: Bounds and Optimal Constructions of Generalized Merge-Convertible Codes for Code Conversion Into LRCs
abstract: Error-correcting codes are essential for ensuring fault tolerance in modern distributed data storage systems. However, in practice, factors such as the failure rates of storage devices can vary significantly over time, resulting in changes to the optimal code parameters. To reduce storage cost while maintaining efficiency, Maturana and Rashmi introduced a theoretical framework known as code conversion, which enables dynamic adjustment of code parameters according to device performance. In this paper, we focus exclusively on the bounds and constructions of generalized merge-convertible codes. First, we establish a new lower bound on the access cost when the final code is an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRC. This bound unifies and generalizes all previously known bounds for merge conversion, where the initial and final codes are either LRCs or MDS codes. We then construct a family of access-optimal MDS convertible codes by leveraging subgroups of the automorphism group of a rational function field. It is worth noting that our construction is also per-symbol read access-optimal. Next, We extend our MDS-based construction to design access-optimal convertible codes that enable conversion between <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs with parameter regimes that have not been previously reported in the literature. Finally, using the parity-check matrix approach, we present a construction of access-optimal convertible codes that enable merge conversion from MDS codes to an <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRC. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit optimal construction of code conversion between MDS codes and LRCs. All of our constructions are performed over finite fields whose sizes grow linearly with the code length.
score_reason: Coding theory for distributed storage; completely unrelated to researcher's interests.

title: Secure Aggregation With an Oblivious Server
abstract: Secure aggregation usually aims at securely computing the sum of the inputs from <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula> users at a server. Noticing that the sum might inevitably reveal information about the inputs (when the inputs are non-uniform) and typically the users (not the server) desire the sum (in applications such as federated learning), we consider a variant of secure aggregation where the server is oblivious, i.e., the server only serves as a communication facilitator/helper to enable the users to securely compute the sum and learns nothing in the process. Our communication protocol involves one round of messages from the users to the server and one round of messages from the server to each user such that in the end each user only learns the sum of all <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula> inputs and the server learns no information about the inputs. For this secure aggregation with an oblivious server problem, we show that to compute 1 bit of the sum securely, each user needs to send at least 1 bit to the server, the server needs to send at least 1 bit to each user, each user needs to hold a key of at least 2 bits, and all users need to collectively hold at least <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula> key bits. In addition, when arbitrary user dropouts are allowed, the optimal performance remains the same, except that the minimum size of the key held by each user increases to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$K$ </tex-math></inline-formula> bits, per sum bit.
score_reason: Information-theoretic cryptography/secure aggregation; unrelated to researcher's interests.

title: Codes Correcting Two Bursts of Exactly b Deletions
abstract: In this paper, we investigate codes designed to correct two bursts of deletions, where each burst has a length of exactly <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$b$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$b\gt 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. The previous best construction, achieved through the syndrome compression technique, had a redundancy of at most <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$7\log n+O\left ({{ \log n/\log \log n }}\right)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> bits. In contrast, our work introduces a novel approach for constructing <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-ary codes that attain a redundancy of at most <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$5\log n+O(\log \log n)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> bits for all <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$b\gt 1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q\ge 2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Additionally, for the case where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$b=1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, we present a new construction of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-ary two-deletion correcting codes with a redundancy of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$5\log n+O(\log \log n)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> bits, for all <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$q\gt 2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>.

title: On Zero Skip-Cost Generalized Fractional-Repetition Codes From Covering Designs
abstract: We study generalized fractional repetition codes that have zero skip cost, and which are based on covering designs. We show that a zero skip cost is always attainable, perhaps at a price of an expansion factor compared with the optimal size of fractional repetition codes based on Steiner systems. We provide three constructions, as well as show non-constructively, that no expansion is needed for all codes based on sufficiently large covering systems.
score_reason: Coding theory / fractional repetition codes; completely unrelated.

title: Random Multiplexing
abstract: As wireless communication applications evolve from traditional multipath environments to high-mobility scenarios like unmanned aerial vehicles, multiplexing techniques have advanced accordingly. Traditional single-carrier frequency-domain equalization (SC-FDE) and orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) have given way to emerging orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) and affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM). These approaches exploit specific channel structures—e.g., Toeplitz-structured multipath channel matrix for OFDM and SC-FDE or doubly selective channels for OTFS and AFDM—to diagonalize or sparsify the effective channel, thereby enabling low-complexity detection. However, their reliance on these structures significantly limits their robustness in dynamic, real-world environments. To address these challenges, this paper studies a random multiplexing technique that is decoupled from the physical channels, thereby enabling its application to arbitrary norm-bounded and spectrally convergent channel matrices. Random multiplexing achieves statistical fading-channel ergodicity for transmitted signals by constructing an equivalent input-isotropic channel matrix in the random transform domain. It guarantees the asymptotic replica MAP bit-error rate (BER) optimality of AMP-type detectors for linear systems with arbitrary norm-bounded, spectrally convergent channel matrices and signaling configurations, under the unique fixed point assumption. A low-complexity cross-domain memory AMP (CD-MAMP) detector is considered for random multiplexing systems, leveraging the sparsity of the time-domain channel and the input isotropy of the equivalent channel. Optimal power allocations are derived to minimize the replica MAP BER and maximize the replica constrained capacity of random multiplexing systems, respectively. The optimal coding principle and replica constrained-capacity optimality of CD-MAMP detector are investigated for random multiplexing systems. Additionally, the versatility of random multiplexing in diverse wireless applications is explored. Numerical results are presented to validate the theoretical findings.
score_reason: Wireless communication multiplexing; completely unrelated.

title: Sliding Secure Symmetric Multilevel Diversity Coding
abstract: Symmetric multilevel diversity coding (SMDC) is a multi-source coding problem where the independent sources are ordered according to their importance. Prior work demonstrated that <italic>superposition coding</italic>, where sources are encoded independently, is optimal. This paper investigates the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(L,s)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> sliding secure SMDC problem, where <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$L$ </tex-math></inline-formula> represents the number of encoders and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$s$ </tex-math></inline-formula> is the security threshold. The security requirement dictates that each source <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{\alpha }$ </tex-math></inline-formula> must be kept perfectly secure if no more than <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\alpha -s$ </tex-math></inline-formula> encoders are accessible. The problem is specialized to the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(L,s)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> <italic>multilevel secret sharing</italic> problem when the first <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$s-1$ </tex-math></inline-formula> sources are constants. For <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$s=1$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, the two problems coincide, and we show that superposition coding is optimal. The rate regions for the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(L,s)=(3,2)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> problems are characterized, which implies that superposition coding is suboptimal for the general case. The core insight for achieving lower rates through joint encoding is leveraging less important sources like <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{\alpha -1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> as secret keys for more important sources like <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{\alpha }$ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Based on this idea, we propose a joint coding scheme that achieves the minimum sum rate of the general <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(L,s)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> multilevel secret sharing problem. Moreover, a pseudo-superposition coding scheme is proposed to achieve the minimum sum rate of the general sliding secure SMDC problem, which uses superposition coding for the <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$s$ </tex-math></inline-formula> sets of sources <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{2}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\cdots $ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{s-1}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(\boldsymbol {X}_{s}, \boldsymbol {X}_{s+1}, \cdots, \boldsymbol {X}_{L})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and joint coding among <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\boldsymbol {X}_{s}, \boldsymbol {X}_{s+1}, \cdots, \boldsymbol {X}_{L}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>.

title: Service Rate Regions of MDS Codes and Fractional Matchings in Quasi-Uniform Hypergraphs
abstract: The Service Rate Region (SRR) is a fundamental performance metric for distributed storage systems with redundancy, quantifying the range of data request patterns that the system can serve concurrently without exceeding the servers’ capacities. Geometrically, the SRR is a convex polytope in <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathbb {R}^{k}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, where each axis corresponds to the request rate for one of <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k$ </tex-math></inline-formula> data objects. This paper focuses on the SRR of systems encoded using a large class of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes. We characterize the axial intercepts of the SRR and derive the smallest standard simplex containing it, demonstrating that the SRR expands strictly as the number of systematic columns in the generator matrix of the code increases. To facilitate this analysis, we develop a graph-theoretic framework that models the SRR as the image of a fractional matching polytope of a quasi-uniform hypergraph. We introduce a novel allocation strategy, <italic>Greedy Matching</italic>, and use it to characterize the SRRs without requiring an exhaustive evaluation of fractional matchings. These findings yield exact SRRs for a wide range of MDS codes and unify previous results regarding systematic and non-systematic constructions. Our work offers both theoretical and practical guidance for designing storage systems with optimized data service.

title: Entanglement Recycling in Two-Step Port-Based Teleportation
abstract: A protocol involving the repetitive (twofold, to be precise) application of PBT protocol to the same resource is studied. The quantities characterizing the resulting protocol, so-called two-step PBT, namely enatnglement fidelity and success probability are provided for two scenarios, relying on application of pretty-good measurement, i.e. deterministic and probabilistic PBT with non-EPR resource. This results show that two-step PBT is an accurate protocol, provided the resource is sufficiently large. In particular, the deterministic two-step PBT obtains fidelity that is remarkably close to the optimal MPBT fidelity for teleportation of two quantum states. Additionally, the recycling fidelity, i.e. the quantity characterizing the degradation of the resource state is calculated for repetitive application of probabilistic protocol, for both EPR and optimized resource, showing that entanglement recycling with two-step PBT is possible in the former case as well.

title: Efficient Approximation of Regularized Relative Entropies and Applications
abstract: The quantum relative entropy is a fundamental quantity in quantum information science, characterizing the distinguishability between two quantum states. However, this quantity is not additive in general for correlated quantum states, necessitating regularization for precise characterization of the operational tasks of interest. Recently, we proposed the study of the regularized relative entropy between two sequences of sets of quantum states in [arXiv: 2411.04035], which captures a general framework for a wide range of quantum information tasks. Here, we show that given suitable structural assumptions and efficient descriptions of the sets, the regularized relative entropy can be efficiently approximated within an additive error by a quantum relative entropy program of polynomial size. This applies in particular to the regularized relative entropy in adversarial quantum channel discrimination. Moreover, we apply the idea of efficient approximation to quantum resource theories. In particular, when the set of interest does not directly satisfy the required structural assumptions, it can be relaxed to one that does. This provides improved and efficient bounds for the entanglement cost of quantum states and channels, entanglement distillation and magic state distillation. Numerical results demonstrate improvements even for the first level of approximation.
